answer: A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. Histories are stored in meadow, checked in yarrow, and quartz publishes each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 6 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm of 1382 identities would post 1135 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
